title: Validate Script (Ctrl+Shift+V) silently does nothing for plain command lists and folder selections
existing_state: validateScriptToolStripMenuItem_Click returns silently when a folder is selected (Form1.cs:5777-5778) and when the editor content isn't detected as a YAML script (Form1.cs:5782-5783). The command is exposed in two always-enabled places — the Edit menu with the global Ctrl+Shift+V shortcut (Form1.Designer.cs:1604-1610) and the editor context menu (ctxValidateScript, Form1.Designer.cs:849, 911-916) — and neither is ever disabled or annotated. So a user with a plain command-list preset presses Validate and gets absolutely no response: no dialog, no output line, no status flash. Because the YAML path pops a success MessageBox with rich feedback (Form1.cs:5793-5812), 'no error appeared' is easy to misread as 'my preset validated clean' when in fact nothing ran. Inline validation has the same silent posture for non-YAML (diagnostics just cleared, UI/ScintillaScriptEditorControl.cs:2247-2257), so no channel ever tells the user their content isn't being checked.
recommendation: Make the no-op states explicit: for non-YAML content show a lightweight info response ('This preset is a plain command list — YAML validation does not apply. Scripts must start with steps:/vars: to be validated.'); for folder selection either validate every YAML preset in the folder (genuinely useful before a folder run) or disable the menu items in the context-menu Opening / DropDownOpening handlers with a tooltip ('Select a preset to validate'). One MessageBox/output-append per branch in validateScriptToolStripMenuItem_Click is enough.
user_benefit: Removes a trust trap: users learn immediately whether their script was actually checked instead of inferring success from silence, and the folder-validation variant would let operators sanity-check an entire folder before a multi-preset run.

evidence.note: Two silent early returns: folder selected, or content not YAML
Ctrl+Shift+V global shortcut on a handler that can silently no-op; item never disabled
YAML path gives rich feedback (success dialog, warnings/errors in output) — silence reads as success
